html:
The walled fortress city of Suwon, south of Seoul, built from 1794 to 1796 by King Jeongjo of Joseon Korea. It is one of the finest works of Korean military building.

Jeongjo built it partly out of love for his father, Crown Prince Sado, whom Jeongjo's grandfather had put to death in 1762. He moved his father's tomb near Suwon and planned the new city as a strong point and perhaps a future capital.

The scholar Jeong Yak-yong drew up the design. He studied Chinese and Western books and used a crane and pulleys that cut the labour of lifting stone. The walls run about 5.7 kilometres, with gates, watchtowers, gun platforms and a floodgate over a stream, built in both stone and brick.

The work was recorded in great detail in a royal report with drawings. When parts of the walls were damaged in the Korean War, they were rebuilt from that record. Hwaseong became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.
sum: The walled fortress city of Suwon, south of Seoul, built from 1794 to 1796 by King Jeongjo of Joseon Korea. It is one of the finest works of Korean military building.
